A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Calibrated Test-Time Guidance for Bayesian Inference. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original results on five Bayesian inference tasks, 100 black-hole imaging instances, and a gradient-estimator variance experiment in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds sampler comparisons, bias and variance analyses, quantitative ImageNet super-resolution results, and qualitative object-count prompt-alignment experiments.

M1.justification: The core estimators and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, but v2 adds deterministic one-step denoise–renoise–denoise proposals in Section 5.3, Equation (21). Appendix I also introduces tile-local likelihood weighting and stitched updates for super-resolution. These change sampling and update procedures; the shortened DDPM inner loop already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates five Bayesian inference tasks and black-hole imaging. v2 retains these and adds 4× ImageNet super-resolution, including evaluation on a 1000-image SR3 list, and text-to-image generation with exact object-count constraints. These introduce distinct natural-image tasks beyond the original coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Langevin+Noisy Classifier, Langevin+REINFORCE, and MCMC No-U-Turn Sampler. New Table 5 compares super-resolution against published DPS, DDRM, RED-diff, C-ΠGDM, MPGD, RB-Modulation, and NDTM results. Figure 6 additionally compares prompt alignment with unguided generation and DPS. The original black-hole comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The original Bayesian benchmark settings and Tables 3–4 are unchanged. v2 adds black-hole renoise configurations using 100 outer steps, alongside the retained 1000-step DDPM configuration, and introduces common-hardware timing and closure-phase/amplitude χ² evaluation. New image experiments specify super-resolution and prompt-alignment protocols, including 2048 candidates over eight steps for super-resolution and additional perceptual metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Task 4 experiment separating estimator bias from variance as K increases (Appendix D, Figure 8), black-hole K-sensitivity analyses using PSNR and χ² (Figures 5 and 9), and DDPM-versus-renoise comparisons. Figure 10 adds a super-resolution trajectory and candidate-diversity case study. The original Gaussian variance analysis and black-hole qualitative comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 95% confidence intervals over 100 tasks in Figures 5 and 9 and specifies 100 repetitions for the new Task 4 bias/variance analysis. Existing table standard deviations and Appendix C's 100-call variance experiment remain. This extends uncertainty reporting without establishing increased repetitions for retained results.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 scores remain, but added baselines change some rankings: Langevin+REINFORCE scores 0.502 on Task 1 versus CBG's 0.505. Table 2 retains the original DDPM result, 26.10 (3.83) dB, and adds renoise results reaching 27.08 (3.74) at K=65536. New super-resolution results include 24.41 PSNR and 40.74 FID, alongside new qualitative findings. These are added configurations and experiments, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A substantially revises the mathematics. Theorem 4.1 replaces its Lipschitz/Taylor argument with an explicit likelihood-maximizer reachability assumption and a new proof. The universal Gaussian-approximation Theorem 4.2 becomes a specific Gaussian-mixture counterexample. Theorem 4.3 gains a revised strict-Jensen proof and a prior-almost-sure constancy condition. These alter formal assumptions, scope and reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim of biased estimators regardless of task, and the conclusion changes universal bias language to 'can be biased,' reflecting the revised theory. Conversely, the abstract and introduction strengthen the black-hole claim from matching state-of-the-art performance to setting a new state-of-the-art PSNR. Fast sampling approximations become an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 retains computational-cost discussion but adds substantive qualifications: renoising is heuristic, measure-zero likelihood support can defeat the sampler, and likelihood-optimizing methods can outperform it on task metrics. Appendix I explains sparse global rewards and the motivation for tiled weighting, and explicitly limits super-resolution comparisons because priors and sampling budgets differ.

D1.justification: v2 announces a code-release URL and documents approximately 140,000 synthetic black-hole training images, the mean-flow model's architecture relationship to DDPM, image checkpoints, preprocessing, reward construction and inference budgets. It adds TITAN RTX timing information; v1's H100 runtime is not directly comparable. Some detail is lost: v1's explicit DDPM inner-step and candidate-count search grids are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Sun et al. (2024)'s related guidance-bias result and prior renoising methods, and adds references supporting mean-flow models, NUTS, image experiments and revised proofs. The existing comparison with Potaptchik et al. is extended to distinguish reuse of deterministic one-step models. These are focused attribution and positioning updates within the retained research framing.

P1.justification: v2 streamlines the introduction and related work, rewrites the black-hole experimental narrative, and moves computational discussion into a dedicated efficiency subsection. It also corrects terminology and affiliation text, updates equal-contribution marking and the publication footer, and renumbers expanded appendices. The overall section sequence and much original prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds plots for sample-count sensitivity and estimator bias/variance, natural-image comparisons, a super-resolution trajectory display, a renoise reconstruction grid, and Table 5. Table 2 gains timing and sampler-variant rows, while Table 1 expands and moves. Existing displays are retained: v1 Figure 5 becomes Figure 7, and Figures 6–7 become Figures 11–12.

improvement.justification: The revised Appendix A addresses important proof and scope problems through explicit assumptions, a concrete counterexample and a strict-Jensen argument. v2 also addresses v1's principal practical bottleneck: its common-hardware Table 2 reports 26.10 dB in 2.9 minutes with renoising versus approximately 23 hours with DDPM. Added comparisons and analyses strengthen the evidence. Fast proposals remain heuristic, and super-resolution comparisons use different priors and budgets, so better image metrics do not establish posterior calibration. Nevertheless, the gains in theoretical reliability and practical usability are substantial.
